claims.text: After a carve-out, the only recurring security inspection of the contractor facility is conducted by the Program Security Officer, who is 'appointed in writing by the appropriate Director CA SAPCO or designee' and exercises responsibilities 'on behalf of the SAPCO' - that is, by the program inspecting itself. Reasoning: DoDM 5205.07-V1 removes the DSS/DCSA inspection and its glossary defines the PSO's appointment chain as internal to the SAP structure.

claims.nodeLabel: Carve-Out Provision (DCSA relief from NISP oversight)
claims.text: A carved-out contractor SAP is the smallest documented configuration in U.S. law in which classified material can be physically held by a private company with no inspection by any official outside the program, no external accreditation of the computers holding the program's data, and no independent counterintelligence reporting line. Reasoning: enumeration of the three functions expressly suspended by DoDM 5205.07-V1 Enclosure 2 para 2.c.

claims.nodeLabel: Cover mechanisms - HVSACO, nicknames, unacknowledged locations
claims.text: THE UNCLASSIFIED WITHHOLDING. DoDM 5205.07 Vol 1, Enclosure 5, para 1 lists when HVSACO is applied, including '(4) To protect information that does not warrant classification under Executive Order 13526' and '(5) When using a SAP nickname for an unacknowledged SAP.' HVSACO is therefore a control expressly designed to hold inside SAP channels material that does NOT meet the standard for classification. Para 1.c requires that on a public release request the originator review the material and either remove the HVSACO marking or 'Inform the requestor of the decision not to release the information, citing an appropriate authority.'

claims.nodeLabel: Cover mechanisms - HVSACO, nicknames, unacknowledged locations
claims.text: DoDM 5205.07 Vol 1, Enclosure 5, para 1.a: 'The purposes of HVSACO are: (1) To preclude the disclosure of general program-related information outside established acknowledged and unacknowledged SAP channels. (2) To minimize OPSEC indicators. (3) To facilitate communication of information within SAPs.' Para 1.b: 'Dissemination of information warranting HVSACO protection will be limited to persons briefed into a SAP and retained within SAP approved channels.'

claims.sourceText: DoDM 5205.07-V1 Enclosure 5 read against E.O. 13526 sections 3.3, 3.5 and 1.8
claims.text: Because HVSACO is expressly not a classification, material bearing it is outside the E.O. 13526 declassification system - it cannot be the subject of a mandatory declassification review, an automatic declassification at 25 years, or a classification challenge. Reasoning: those remedies operate only on classified national security information.

claims.nodeLabel: DCSA as DoD Cognizant Security Office under the NISP
claims.text: DoDM 5205.07 Vol 1, Enclosure 2, para 2.b (then DSS, now DCSA): 'Issues facility security clearances (FCLs) for defense contractors performing on all DoD classified contracts, to include contractors performing on DoD SAPs.' Facility clearance issuance is NOT carved out -- only inspection, IS authorization and CI cross-sharing are. A carved-out SAP contractor site still has a DCSA-issued FCL and therefore still exists in DCSA's facility records.

claims.nodeLabel: DCSA as DoD Cognizant Security Office under the NISP
claims.text: Because the FCL function survives a carve-out (DoDM V1 Encl 2 para 2.b) while inspection does not, DCSA's facility clearance database remains the one government-wide index that lists a carved-out SAP contractor location as a cleared facility, even when no inspector may enter it. That makes FCL records a discovery surface that the carve-out does not close. Reasoning stated.

claims.nodeLabel: DoDM 5205.07 - DoD SAP Security Manual (Volumes 1-4)
claims.text: THE CARVE-OUT'S OPERATIONAL CONTENT. DoDM 5205.07 Vol 1, Enclosure 2, para 2 (Director, DSS): 'Unless a carve-out provision is approved by the Secretary of Defense or the Deputy Secretary of Defense: (1) Performs SAP security inspections at cleared defense contractor locations in accordance with this volume, Reference (f), and the government contracting activity's completed DD Form 254 ... (2) Authorizes classified contractor SAP information systems (ISs) and the introduction of guest systems in contractor SAP facilities (SAPFs). (3) Coordinates with the designated counterintelligence (CI) component to provide cross-sharing of threat and incident information affecting the security of the facility or its defense information or cleared personnel.' A carve-out removes all three functions at once: physical inspection, IT accreditation, and CI information sharing.

There is an explicit, standing policy channel for patents arising inside special access programs, delegated to each cognizant-authority SAP central office.

claims.nodeLabel: DoDM 5205.07 - DoD SAP Security Manual (Volumes 1-4)
claims.text: WHISTLEBLOWING IS ROUTED BACK INSIDE. Vol 1, Enclosure 4, para 3: 'Government and industry FWAC SAP reporting involving SAP information will be accomplished through SAP channels. Collateral FWAC reporting channels must not be used for SAP information. b. The PSO will provide the telephone number for the current FWAC hotline for reporting SAP information. FWAC reporting information will be conspicuously posted in the SAP workspace. c. Employees do not need management approval before making reports.' Fraud, waste, abuse and corruption inside a SAP may not be reported through the ordinary DoD IG hotline; it must go through a SAP-channel hotline whose number is issued by the program's own security officer.

claims.nodeLabel: DoDM 5205.07 - DoD SAP Security Manual (Volumes 1-4)
claims.text: Vol 1, Enclosure 4, para 4: 'The CUA documents areas of authorities and responsibilities between cognizant security offices (CSOs) when they share the same SAPF. ... The first CSO in an area, unless otherwise agreed upon, will be considered the host CSO responsible for all security oversight.' And, critically: 'For CUAs, the responsible organization will be identified for executing security cognizance with a carved-out SAP.' Multiple SAPs -- including carved-out ones -- can lawfully co-occupy one accredited facility under a written host/tenant agreement.

The 'NISPOM Supplement Overprint' -- the historic classified-annex mechanism for SAP industrial security -- was folded into this public manual in 2015.

b.label: Carve-Out Provision (DCSA relief from NISP oversight)

edges.label: defines and operates the carve-out
edges.note: The Manual is where the carve-out is defined and where it operates. Volume 1's glossary: 'carve-out. A provision approved by the Secretary or Deputy Secretary of Defense that relieves DSS of its NISP obligation to perform industrial security oversight.' Enclosure 2 para 2 carries the operational form of the same provision, and Volume 1 also states that inspections 'will be coordinated among the SAPCOs and DSS when not carved out' - which is the sentence establishing that a carved-out SAP is not so coordinated. Quotations are the verbatim ones already recorded on this node.

b.label: DCSA as DoD Cognizant Security Office under the NISP

edges.label: relieves it of oversight
edges.note: The carve-out's effect runs against this body: the Manual's own definition is that the provision 'relieves DSS of its NISP obligation to perform industrial security oversight'. DSS is the predecessor of DCSA, which now holds the cognizant-security-office role under the NISP. The Manual is the instrument by which the oversight body is stood down for a given programme.

b.label: DoD Special Access Program Central Office (DoD SAPCO)

edges.label: assigns it the patent and inspection roles
edges.note: Volume 1 Enclosure 4 para 7: 'PATENTS AND INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY. The CA SAPCO will develop procedures for processing patents and intellectual property involving SAP(s).' Volume 1 also routes inspections through the SAPCOs jointly with DSS where a programme is not carved out. Both are verbatim from this node's recorded quotations, and the patents provision is the one that matters most to this board: it is an explicit channel for intellectual property arising inside a special access programme.
